# Architecture Decision Records

Curated by Skill Harbor: a workflow for capturing architectural decisions as they happen, so they stop living only in chat threads, PR comments, or someone's memory. Uses the lightweight ADR format (context, decision, alternatives considered with pros/cons and explicit why-not, consequences split into positive, negative, and risks) stored as numbered markdown files in docs/adr/, with an index README and a blank template for manual use. The skill watches for decision moments in conversation, both explicit ("let's go with X", "record this as an ADR") and implicit (comparing two frameworks and reaching a conclusion, choosing an auth strategy), then gathers the context, documents the rejected alternatives, and presents a draft for your approval before writing anything. Covers the ADR lifecycle (proposed, accepted, deprecated, superseded by a newer ADR), what makes a good ADR (specific, readable in two minutes, honest about trade-offs, never an essay), and which decision categories deserve one: technology choices, architecture patterns, API design, data modeling, infrastructure, security, and testing. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: pure guidance, nothing to install; it asks for your confirmation before creating any files, and trivial decisions (naming, formatting) do not deserve an ADR. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
